Log your fill-ups in seconds. Automatically calculate your fuel economy (MPG, L/100km, km/L) and track your cost per unit over time.

Keep a detailed history of oil changes, tire rotations, brake jobs, and general repairs. Fuel Log will even alert you when your next maintenance interval is approaching.

Last month, we published our most ambitious update! 

However, many features were broken or underdeveloped, so we have scaled back, and refocused on quality over quantity 

Trends & Charts: We completely redesigned the charts screen! 
You can now filter data by specific timeframes (3 months, 6 months, 1 year, etc.), scroll horizontally through your data without it feeling cramped, and view a brand-new statistics summary card for deeper insights into your vehicle's efficiency and costs.

- Passport: We’ve temporarily removed the "Passports" feature to declutter the app while we redesign it from the ground up.

- Security Fix: Fixed an annoying bug where Face ID / Touch ID would wipe out your unsaved data if the app locked while you were logging a fill-up. Your unsaved data and open screens are now safely preserved behind the lock screen.

- Maintenance Reminders: Fixed an issue where archived vehicles were still sending maintenance reminders. You will now only be notified for your active vehicles.

- Currency Formatting: Fixed a bug where the Total Cost field would sometimes display three decimal places instead of standard currency formatting.

results.releaseNotes:
Hello. I managed to do 5 pull-ups.

Anyway, this update adds a nice new feature along with a few bug fixes.

● Added the ability to select the displayed vehicle from a list
● Fixed an issue that could cause the app to crash right after launch

Fuel Record allows you to register an unlimited number of vehicles, and quite a few users actually have multiple vehicles registered. However, switching between vehicles was previously limited to moving through them one by one using the left and right buttons. If you had many vehicles registered, this meant tapping repeatedly to get to the one you wanted, which wasn’t very convenient.

In fact, I’ve received requests from users asking to select vehicles from a list, and this update adds that feature.

If you have multiple vehicles registered, tap the vehicle name at the top of the screen (the part that shows something like “XXX Records”). This will open a menu where you’ll find a new option called “Select Vehicle.” Tapping that will show a list of your registered vehicles, and you can choose one from there.

I think this will be especially useful for those who have many vehicles registered, so please give it a try.

Also, regarding the issue where the app could occasionally crash right after launch, I’m still investigating it. The previous update improved things quite a bit, but it seems the issue can still occur in rare cases. I’m sorry to those who have experienced this.

In this update, I’ve implemented an additional fix, so I believe it should be further improved, but I’ll continue to keep a close eye on it for a while.

If you enjoy using the app, please consider upgrading. Reviews are also very much appreciated.
Well then again!
